arguments.conclusion: The SLR and LCR are contradictory regulations that constrain bank lending.
source_speech_filenames: 20260218_Get Ready for Bank Deregulation.txt
arguments.premise_synthesis: SLR is a hard cap on total assets relative to capital, regardless of risk. LCR requires banks to hold a certain amount of high-quality liquid assets, primarily treasuries. These two rules together force banks to hold treasuries but then limit their ability to hold anything else.
arguments.conclusion_supported: The contradiction between SLR and LCR constrains bank lending, establishing a regulatory barrier that removal of the SLR could alleviate.

source_speech_filenames: 20260218_Get Ready for Bank Deregulation.txt
relationship_explanations: The speech directly argues that removing the supplementary leverage ratio will allow banks to buy unlimited treasuries and lend more, lowering Treasury yields and government borrowing costs, which is the core proposition of CC39 that bank deregulation (SLR removal) is the most effective solution to stimulate growth and prevent crisis.
